clue.text: Developed into hard worker outside academic stream

indicators.note: the worker's letters sit outside, wrapping round the stream

parts.note: a bee is proverbially busy, a byword for hard work
the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge, a university town

explanation.surface: A diligent student, out by the river at university, grew into something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Became is the past tense of become, meaning grew or turned into something, as in 'developed into'.

clue.text: Part that extends over prow's possibly this

definitions.text: Part that extends over prow's possibly this

indicators.note: the part stretches across, enclosing the shuffled letters

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

indicators.note: 'possibly' says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A description of the ship's spar that juts out beyond the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay, so 'this' points back at the answer described.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is the spar projecting forward from a sailing ship's stem, extending beyond the bow.

clue.text: Priest, generally, converted sons with force

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman forcibly brings his sons round to the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A confessor is the cleric who hears confessions, usually but not always a priest, hence 'generally'.

clue.text: Screening male in role of Lear, for example

parts.note: 'as' means playing the part of
Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: An actor auditioning for King Lear is being vetted.
explanation.definitionFit: Masking means hiding or covering from view, as a screen does.

clue.text: Rescues Las Vegas drunk

indicators.note: being drunk means being jumbled and unsteady, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone saves a city of gamblers from intoxication.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage is to save goods or property from loss or wreck, so salvages works as a verb meaning rescues.

clue.text: These parts of newspaper are, in brief, central for dreadful lady reader

definitions.text: These parts of newspaper are, in brief, central for dreadful lady reader

parts.words: These parts of newspaper are, in brief, central for dreadful lady reader
parts.note: the short form of the answer is ADS, and AD sits in the middle of each of the words dreadful, lady and reader

explanation.walkthrough: Read the middles: dreADful, lADy, reADer each centre on the same two letters, so three of the abbreviated items sit there.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid notices in a paper promoting goods or services are commercial announcements of this kind.

clue.text: Gallery section for engraver and artist

indicators.note: a section of the run of words is cut out to supply the letters

explanation.surface: An exhibition space has a dedicated area for printmakers and painters.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform along the outside of a house, and gallery is an old name for such a porch.

clue.text: Interrogate as gaoler, extremely badly

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ill means badly, as in 'ill-treated'

explanation.surface: A jailer questions a prisoner very harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaoler is the British spelling of jailer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them intensely and at length, like a police interrogation.

clue.text: Cruel person lives in depressed time

indicators.note: the word for lives is placed in the middle of the gloomy-time pair

parts.note: depressed means sad
'is' can mean exists or lives

explanation.surface: A cruel character lives through a period of gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others, the very picture of cruelty.

clue.text: Hamlet's problem, having sorted out vice inside head

indicators.note: sorting out the letters puts them in a new order

parts.note: a ness is a headland or promontory, as in Dungeness

explanation.surface: The prince's trouble came from wickedness lodged in his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the mind; it is a headland, NESS, as in place names like Dungeness on the English coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet famously dithers over avenging his father, so his flaw is an inability to make up his mind.

clue.text: Entertains in a way, with quartet of players around one

indicators.note: the players' letters go around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: the four players at a bridge table are West, North, East and South, abbreviated W, N, E, S
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A string quartet plays around a solo performer to amuse an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The four bridge seats are named by compass points, so a 'quartet of players' gives four single letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: To wine someone, as in 'wine and dine', is to treat them to drinks, one particular way of hosting a guest.

clue.text: Despicable people introduced to new editor? Forget it!

indicators.note: the despicable people are brought into the middle of the pair of letters that follow

parts.note: vermin is a contemptuous term for loathsome people

explanation.surface: Undesirables are presented to the incoming editor, who brushes the whole thing aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive exclamation telling someone not to bother, which is the same as saying 'forget it'.

clue.text: Destruction of empires, from which one may draw certain conclusions

definitions.text: from which one may draw certain conclusions
definitions.note: a definition by description of a noun: the thing reasoning starts from

indicators.note: destroying the word breaks it up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Historians study the fall of empires and draw firm lessons from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a proposition assumed in an argument, the starting point from which a logical inference is drawn.

clue.text: Runs low joints, and is persistently annoying

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
ankles are the joints lowest on the body

explanation.surface: A jogger's sore lower joints keep nagging at them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles continues to cause lingering bitterness or irritation, the sense of nagging annoyance.

clue.text: Lack of importance within certain sign, if I cancel

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follows, spanning them

explanation.surface: If I strike out a particular sign, it would hardly matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificance is the quality of being trivial or of no consequence, exactly a lack of weight or importance.

clue.text: Standard note covering disorderly interior

indicators.note: in a down answer the note sits on top, covering the rest

parts.note: C is a musical note

indicators.note: disorderly means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regulation memo deals with a messy inside space.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a principle or benchmark by which something is judged, a yardstick.

clue.text: Potential husbands with match in mind

parts.note: men are the eligible husbands of the surface
to tally is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: A matchmaker considers which suitors would suit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentally means in or by the mind, an adverb for thinking without outward expression.

clue.text: Unfinished research I'm doing badly? Dons control it

indicators.note: done badly means botched, so the letters are scrambled
a word left unfinished loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A researcher confesses their academic work is going poorly, while university dons supervise it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university lecturers but here means Mafia bosses. Drop H from RESEARCH to get RESEARC, add IM and DOING, and 'badly' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mafia families, run by their dons, are the classic example of a criminal syndicate.

clue.text: Divided in the way shown below

parts.note: 'as' means in the manner of
'under' marks what follows below, as in 'see under'

explanation.surface: A document points the reader to a split described further down the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart or into separate pieces, as in 'torn asunder'.

clue.text: Person removing some nails, perhaps, from old vessel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who clips, for instance trimming fingernails
second meaning: a fast nineteenth-century sailing ship

explanation.surface: A manicurist works aboard a historic ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipper ships like the Cutty Sark were swift merchant sailing ships, and anyone who trims is also a clipper.

clue.text: Primate and historian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small tree-dwelling ape
second meaning: Edward ..., author of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could be an archbishop, but here it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The ape and the eighteenth-century English writer of Roman history share this name.

clue.text: Comprehend where setter's skill is shown around end of crossword

indicators.note: the first part is placed round the letter

parts.note: a compiler's craft shows in a clue, so 'in clue'

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A setter's artistry is on display in this puzzle, if only you can grasp it.
explanation.definitionFit: Comprehend in its older sense means to contain or take in, which is what include means.

clue.text: Influence foolish person had over union leader in strike

indicators.note: the letter goes in the middle of the fool

parts.note: a clot is a British word for a fool

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A union boss has power over a fool during an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also means a strike or blow, as the clue's last word suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for power or sway, especially political influence.

clue.text: Demanding leave for player concealing dope

indicators.note: the stage direction hides the information inside it

parts.note: Exit is the stage direction telling an actor to leave
dope is slang for information, as is gen

explanation.surface: A footballer demands to leave the club while hiding a drugs secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or urgent, making heavy demands on someone, so it matches the adjective.

clue.text: Before big game, initiate check for drugs, perhaps

indicators.note: the initiating word is placed ahead of the game in the answer

parts.note: to blood someone is to initiate them, from smearing new hunters with blood
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: An athlete is introduced to doping control ahead of a major match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a time phrase for the surface but tells you which piece comes first. A Test match is a long international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood sample can be screened for banned substances, one use among many for such a medical analysis.

clue.text: Container repeatedly broken in outskirts of Philadelphia

indicators.note: the city is broken twice: once to take its outskirts, again to rearrange them
only the edges of the city are kept, the middle stretch dropped

explanation.surface: A bottle keeps getting smashed in the suburbs of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of PHILADELPHIA are PHIL at the front and A at the back; the second break rearranges PHILA.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle, typically for medicine, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Authenticate a cut in pay, or no change

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to certify a document as a notary does

definitions.text: a cut in pay, or no change
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as three words

explanation.surface: Workers want written confirmation of whether their salary will fall or stay frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into NOT A RISE, a fair summary of either bad pay outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary public certifies signatures and documents, and to have something notarised is to make it officially valid.

clue.text: Berry, oddly, put in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the joining word goes in, placed inside the odd letters of the fruit
the odd-numbered letters of the following word are taken

parts.note: 'put' stands loosely for 'added' or 'plus', which is what the word 'and' means; the blog reads it this way too

explanation.surface: Someone drops a berry into a glass of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: No 'and' is printed in the clue: 'put in' means added inside, and 'and' is the word for added, a loose step the blog accepts.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, so it is an intoxicating beverage.
